items.name: Game dev support (Programming)
items.can: General feature implementation in Unity. We use generative AI to move fast, and include a ReadMe (spec and handover notes). No spec document needed — tell us the gist of what you want and we'll shape it together as we go.
items.ng: We can't work with engines other than Unity.

items.name: Game dev support (Planning & specs)
items.can: Game concept planning and spec documents. Specs are shared in Excel, ready to use for production as-is.
items.ng: We don't do scenario or story writing.

items.name: Game dev support (UI design)
items.can: Simple, readable UI parts — buttons, frames, panels — made in Photoshop. We can also integrate them into Unity.
items.ng: We can't draw illustrations. UI that needs character art or elaborate decoration is out of scope.

items.name: Game design consultation
items.can: How to make the systems fun, how to present your theme — we'll think it through together on an online call. Half-finished ideas, or none at all yet, are both fine.
items.ng: We don't take adult (erotic) titles or visual novels.

items.name: 3D models for games
items.can: Models made with generative AI, adjusted in Blender, then delivered. Simple shapes only.
items.ng: High-poly models and complex rigging or animation are out of scope.
items.at: Because generative AI is used, they must be disclosed as AI-generated content if you release on Steam.

items.name: Images for Steam and other stores
items.can: We take in-game screenshots and edit them in Photoshop and similar tools into capsule images and banners, all sized to Steam's requirements.
items.ng: We can't draw illustrations. Hand-drawn key visuals are out of scope.

items.name: Trailer

unit.l: 1 min + capture assets made for it

items.can: We capture your game and edit it in Premiere Pro into a simple, easy-to-follow trailer.
items.ng: Elaborate motion graphics, live-action filming, and original music are out of scope. Music will be royalty-free tracks or assets you provide.

items.name: Debugging & playtesting
items.can: We actually play your game to find bugs and report them with steps to reproduce. We'll also point out spots that could be better, from a game creator's point of view.
items.ng: Please ask separately about setting up automated tests.

items.name: All-in: planning → development → release
items.can: Everything from planning and Unity development to release on Steam / iOS / Google Play. Ad implementation and placement are available too.
items.ng: Scenario writing and full-scale illustration or sound are out of scope (please provide them, or outsource them separately).
items.at: Because of scheduling, we can only take a limited number of these at a time. Please get in touch first.

items.name: Online multiplayer implementation
items.can: Online versus and co-op in Unity. We use generative AI, backed by our experience actually shipping an online co-op game.
items.at: The work involved in networking varies a lot with the spec. Treat the price as a rough guide.

items.name: Bug fixing & optimization for existing games
items.can: Investigating and fixing bugs in Unity projects, and optimizing slow parts, with the help of generative AI.
items.at: You'll need to share the full project. “Small” covers investigation and finding the cause only; fixes are charged separately.

items.name: Technical lessons & mentoring
items.can: How to use Unity, how to think about implementation, and how to run solo development — taught from our own hands-on experience, over online calls.
items.ng: We won't do school assignments for you.

items.name: Steam release: done for you or with you
items.can: Steamworks setup, store page creation, build submission, and review handling. We can do it for you, or work through it together over screen share so you learn how.
items.at: You'll need to pay the Steam Direct fee and register your own bank account and tax information.
